title: The nine reminders
hook: Marcus lists nine things to recall when offended: we're made for each other, they act from beliefs, we err too (Meditations 11.18)

segments.voice: Yesterday: kind to everyone. Your line was theirs, and mine. Who got your kindness, and what did they do with it? Day six hundred twenty-four.

Someone offends you, and the old script starts running: how dare they, who do they think they are, wait till I tell everyone. Marcus wrote a different script. It's a long entry, and it's numbered, first, second, third, like a checklist a pilot runs before takeoff, item by item. He wrote it to read when someone offended him, a list to run before the reply goes out. Today: the nine reminders.
screen: `HOW DARE THEY.` → `A NUMBERED CHECKLIST.` → `THE NINE REMINDERS.`

segments.voice: First, about them. One: we're made for one another. Two: think what these people are like at the table, in bed, and what beliefs are driving them. Three: if they're right, don't complain; if they're wrong, it's unwillingly, out of ignorance. No soul, Marcus says, is willingly cut off from the truth. Second, about you. Four: you do plenty of wrong yourself, and even when you don't, you have the tendency, held back only by fear or concern for your reputation. Five: you don't even know for certain that they're doing wrong; many things are done for reasons you can't see. Six: when you're furious, remember that life is a moment, and soon we'll all be laid out. Third, about the anger. Seven: it isn't their acts that disturb us; those live in them. It's our own judgments. Take away the judgment that it's terrible, and the anger goes with it. Eight: our anger and grief hurt us more than the things that caused them. Fourth, the last. Nine: kindness is invincible, if it's real, not a fake smile or an act. What can the most violent person do if you stay kind, and at the very moment they try to harm you, gently say: no, my child, we were made for something else; you won't harm me, you're harming yourself, my child. Then Marcus adds a tenth, as a gift, he says, from the leader of the Muses: to expect bad people not to do wrong is madness.
screen: `ONE TO THREE: KIN, BELIEFS, IGNORANCE.` · `FOUR TO SIX: ME TOO, UNSURE, BRIEF.` · `SEVEN AND EIGHT: MY JUDGMENT, MY ANGER.` · `NINE: KINDNESS IS INVINCIBLE.` · then, large: `NINE REMINDERS.`

segments.voice: Settle, and breathe. Bring to mind one person who offended you recently. Now, slowly, run the nine. We're made for each other. They act from their beliefs. If they're wrong, it's unwilling. I've done the same. I can't be sure. Life is short. It's my judgment that hurts. My anger hurts more. Kindness can't be beaten. Let each one land for a breath, and notice which one loosens the knot. The bell holds the time.
The nine reminders. Marcus's numbered checklist for when someone offends you, from we're made for each other to kindness is invincible. Today's word.
Your line: nine reminders. Next time someone offends you, run even three of them before you answer. Day six hundred twenty-four.

howItsDone: Some readers of the Meditations copy out the nine reminders and reread them when someone has offended them, often before replying.

fork.setup: someone tries to harm you, right now, in front of you. you're Marcus with reminder nine. what do you say?
options: gently: no, my child, we were made for something else; you're harming yourself.
fork.reveal: kindness is invincible if it's genuine, he writes, and gives himself those very words for the moment the other tries to harm him.

original.note: Greek: unconquerable, invincible. Marcus's word for genuine kindness in reminder nine.

trapdoor: what you thought: count to ten.
what it means: nine reasons, thought through, to drain anger, ending with kindness as the one answer that can't be beaten.
what a scholar hears: Marcus numbers the reminders himself, first, second, and so on; the leader of the Muses who gives the tenth is Apollo.

notes: 11.18 paraphrased in full: (1) relation to men, made for one another (with the ram/bull image omitted); (2) what they are at table, in bed, compelled by opinions; (3) if right, no complaint; if not, involuntarily, in ignorance; (4) you too do wrong, or have the disposition, restrained by cowardice or reputation; (5) you don't know they are doing wrong; (6) life is a moment, we are soon laid out; (7) it's our opinions, not their acts, that disturb us; (8) anger and vexation cause more pain than the acts; (9) benevolence is invincible if genuine; 'Not so, my child...'; tenth gift from the leader of the Muses (Apollo Musagetes). Confirm order and wording.
'One of the longest entries in the Meditations' is a safe description of 11.18; confirm.
Editor review (year 2): removed the unsourced 'one of the longest entries in the Meditations' and the 'most of us' hook opener; 'the strongest' became 'the last'.
